originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq, S&P fall over 1%, end lower for week as chip selloff broadens
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the Nasdaq and S&P (two important groups of stocks) fell by more than 1% today, which means the value of many stocks went down. This happened because some technology companies that make computer chips, which are important for artificial intelligence, are doing poorly and losing value. At the same time, energy companies are doing well because oil prices are rising due to problems in the Middle East. This mix of good and bad news is making investors feel uncertain, especially since some companies like Netflix are predicting weaker future performance, which is also affecting the market. Overall, this uncertainty is causing the stock market to end the week on a low note.

originalTitle: Reliance Retail Q1 revenue rises, but profit falls as e-commerce weighs
simplifiedContent: Reliance Retail, a big retail company, had a mixed first quarter. Their total sales went up by 8.2%, which is a good sign, but their profit actually decreased by 14.2%. This decrease in profit happened because the company is spending a lot on its online shopping business, which is affecting its overall margins. Another part of the company, Reliance Consumer, did very well and saw its sales more than double, thanks to strong performance in areas like groceries and electronics. This news matters because it shows how Reliance Retail is doing and how its investments in e-commerce are impacting its bottom line.

originalTitle: JSW Steel’s profit doubles on revenue growth, beats estimates
simplifiedContent: JSW Steel, a company that produces steel, made a profit of Rs 4,696 crore in the quarter ending June, which is more than double what they made last year. This is due to an increase in sales (called revenue growth) and lower costs for borrowing money (finance costs). The company's total sales rose by 10% to Rs 47,364 crore, while their expenses only went up by less than 4%. This combination of higher sales and lower expenses helped the company perform well financially. The company's good performance is significant because it exceeded expectations, which can impact investor confidence and the company's overall value.

originalTitle: Netflix shares tumble 13% after weak sales forecast, hit 22-month low
simplifiedContent: Netflix's stock price dropped by 12.6% to its lowest point in 22 months. This happened because the company said it doesn't expect to make as much money as people thought it would, even though its recent earnings were what was expected. The company's revenue, or the amount of money it makes, is growing more slowly than before. This is partly because its original content, like TV shows and movies, isn't performing as well as hoped, which is affecting the company's overall value. As a result, investors are selling their Netflix stocks, causing the price to fall.

originalTitle: Sebi clears automatic SWP, STP mandates for demat mutual fund holdings
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, has made a new rule for people who invest in mutual funds through a demat account. Before this rule, investors could only set up automatic instructions for mutual funds that were not held in a demat account. Now, investors can set up automatic instructions, such as systematic withdrawal plans (SWP) and systematic transfer plans (STP), for mutual funds held in their demat account. This change makes it easier for investors to manage their mutual fund investments. It matters because it gives investors more flexibility and convenience in handling their investments.

originalTitle: Pulse of the Street: Earnings sentiment rescues volatile week; real test ahead
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the stock market: the main Indian stock market indexes, called the Sensex and Nifty, went up a bit this week. The Sensex rose by 0.75% and the Nifty by 0.53%, which means the value of the stocks in these indexes increased slightly. Most of the increase happened on Friday, when the Nifty jumped 1.1% and the Sensex went up 1.25%. This is a good sign for investors, as it shows that the market is recovering from some previous ups and downs. The Sensex even reached its highest point since June 12, 2026, which is a positive note to end the week.
